problems.name: Matching
problems.definition: Find a set of edges with no shared endpoints. Maximum matching maximizes its size; maximal matching only requires that no edge can be added.
problems.quality: α ≥ 1: output size ≥ OPT / α. Value estimation and explicit edge output are different tasks.
problems.variants: Maximum / maximal · value / explicit edges · weighted / unweighted

problems.name: Weighted matching
problems.definition: Find vertex-disjoint edges maximizing total weight. Edge weights and weights on matched vertices define distinct setups.
problems.quality: Retained weight β=E[ALG]/OPT, or approximation factor α=OPT/ALG; state the convention per figure.
problems.variants: Edge weights / vertex weights · approximation / exact · arrival and revision rules

problems.name: Maximal independent set
problems.definition: Find an independent vertex set that cannot be extended by adding another vertex. This is a maximality task, not optimization of the largest independent set.
problems.quality: For construction: exact maximality. For size estimation: multiplicative error relative to a specified or algorithm-chosen MIS.
problems.variants: Construction / size estimation · arbitrary MIS / greedy MIS under an order

problems.name: Correlation clustering
problems.definition: Partition a signed graph into clusters. Minimize disagreements or maximize agreements, with the objective and the treatment of missing edges stated separately.
problems.quality: Minimization uses α≥1 with cost≤α·OPT. Maximization uses retained fraction β≤1 with value≥β·OPT; these guarantees are not interchangeable.
problems.variants: Min disagreements / max agreements · complete signed / sparse signed network · weighted / unweighted

problems.name: Edge coloring
problems.definition: Assign colors to edges so that edges sharing an endpoint receive different colors. Each color class is a matching.
problems.quality: Use palette size q, often expressed in terms of maximum degree Δ. A Δ+1 palette is different from an approximation to χ′(G).
problems.variants: Palette q · simple graphs / multigraphs · list coloring

problems.name: Vertex coloring
problems.definition: Assign colors to vertices so that adjacent vertices receive different colors. Each color class is an independent set.
problems.quality: Use palette size q, such as Δ+1, or an explicitly defined approximation to χ(G). These are separate objectives.
problems.variants: Palette q · ordinary / list coloring · graph class

models.name: Dynamic
models.definition: Maintain a solution while edges are inserted or deleted; for signed graphs, updates may flip labels.
models.settings: Fully / partially dynamic · amortized / worst-case · adversary · recourse
models.unit: Time per update; also query time and recourse

access.operations: Edge insertion/deletion; signed settings may flip an edge label
access.resource: Time per update; report amortized or worst case per setting

models.name: Streaming
models.definition: Process a sequence of graph updates using limited memory, with a specified number of passes.
models.settings: Passes · edge / vertex arrival · order · insertion-only / turnstile

access.operations: Edge or vertex arrivals; insertion-only and turnstile are distinct settings
access.resource: Memory in bits or words at a stated number of passes

models.name: Online
models.definition: Make decisions as input arrives without knowing future arrivals. The arrival process, information revealed, and permitted revisions are specified separately for each submodel.
models.settings: Edge / vertex arrivals · adversarial / random order · irrevocable / preemptive / recourse · weighted / unweighted
models.unit: Competitive guarantee against a stated offline optimum; permitted recourse separately

access.operations: Reveal arriving edges or vertices and their allowed incident information; irrevocable decisions, preemption, or bounded revisions as stated
access.resource: Competitive guarantee under the stated arrival and decision rules; recourse when allowed

models.name: LCA
models.definition: Answer a requested local part of one globally consistent solution, using oracle probes to the input graph.
models.settings: Probe access · preprocessing · shared randomness · state · query sequence
models.unit: Probes or time per local answer; space tracked separately

access.operations: Answer a requested vertex/edge of one consistent solution by graph probes
access.resource: Probes per answer; preprocessing and state per setting

models.name: LOCAL
models.definition: Vertices communicate synchronously with neighbors. Messages are unbounded; after r rounds a vertex sees only its radius-r neighborhood.
models.settings: Identifiers · randomization · success probability · degree Δ

access.resource: Communication rounds; degree and probability per setting

models.name: MPC
models.definition: Distribute the graph across machines and communicate in synchronous rounds under per-machine and total memory budgets.
models.settings: Local memory · total memory · component stability · randomness
models.unit: Rounds at fixed local and total space

access.operations: Synchronous machine communication with local and total memory caps
access.resource: Rounds at the memory budget stated in the setting

models.name: Adjacency-list queries
models.definition: Learn graph neighborhoods through adjacency-list or adjacency-array probes, with the allowed degree and neighbor operations stated per setting.
models.settings: Neighbor queries · degree queries · adaptive/non-adaptive · explicit/value output

access.operations: Degree and indexed-neighbor access only when the setting allows them
access.resource: Oracle queries; running time separately if stated

models.name: Adjacency-matrix queries
models.definition: Inspect entries of the adjacency matrix, usually by pair queries, with the allowed adaptivity and output task stated per setting.
models.unit: Matrix entries queried and running time

access.resource: Pair queries; running time separately if stated

models.name: Combined / other queries
models.definition: Use multiple oracle types, a same-cluster oracle, or a related communication/query interface. These settings remain separate from pure list and pure matrix access.
models.settings: Combined oracles · pair communication · same-cluster oracle · value/output task
models.unit: Queries, rounds, communication, and running time

access.operations: Exact oracle combination or communication interface specified by each setting
access.resource: Queries, communication bits, or rounds as stated

models.name: Stochastic
models.definition: Algorithms under a stated random-input or noisy-observation model. Independent edge survival, supplied random graphs, planted partitions, and semirandom additions are distinct setups.
models.settings: Independent edge survival · random graphs · persistent noisy queries · planted/semirandom inputs
models.unit: Setting-specific query, iteration, density, approximation, or failure-probability guarantee

access.interface: Stated random input or noisy observations
access.operations: Edge tests, supplied random graphs, persistent pair queries, or semirandom inputs as labeled
access.resource: Queries, iterations, solution density, or failure probability; incompatible units remain separate

relations.label: MIS → maximal matching
relations.formula: Run MIS on the line graph L(G).
relations.detail: One vertex of L(G) represents one edge of G; adjacency means shared endpoints. An MIS in L(G) is a maximal matching in G, hence a 2-approximation to maximum matching.
relations.overhead: n becomes m; maximum degree is at most 2Δ−2 for a simple graph with edges. Query, update, and memory costs must be translated.

relations.label: Vertex coloring → edge coloring
relations.detail: A proper q-vertex-coloring of L(G) gives a proper q-edge-coloring of G. A generic (Δ(L(G))+1)-coloring yields at most 2Δ−1 colors.
relations.overhead: L(G) has m vertices and can have Θ(mΔ) edges. A reduction in one model need not preserve another model’s resource bound.

relations.label: Vertex coloring → MIS
relations.formula: Process q color classes in order.
relations.detail: All vertices of the current color with no selected neighbor join the independent set. Proper coloring prevents conflicts within a phase; after the final phase the set is maximal.
relations.overhead: Given a q-coloring, O(q) additional LOCAL rounds. This is a direct construction, not a claim that the overhead is optimal.

relations.label: Edge coloring → maximal matching
relations.formula: Process q edge-color classes in order.
relations.detail: For each color, add edges whose endpoints are still unmatched. Edges of that color are disjoint, so they can act together. The final matching is maximal.
relations.overhead: Given a q-edge-coloring, O(q) additional LOCAL rounds; the result is a 2-approximation to maximum matching.

relations.label: Random greedy MIS → Pivot
relations.formula: Greedy MIS vertices become Pivot centers.
relations.detail: On the positive-edge graph, process a random vertex order. Selected pivots form the corresponding greedy MIS; assign each nonpivot to its earliest selected neighbor. This recovers Pivot’s clustering.
relations.overhead: Needs the random order and eliminator assignments, not an arbitrary MIS. Dynamic implementations also maintain auxiliary neighborhood data.
